description:
REVALIDATED 2026-08-23 with a fresh end-to-end run on current develop. The public corpus still has zero plain tpcds bundles (only tpcds_obt=5 and tpcdi=9) across 207 bundles.

MEASURED COST OF w2 -- this is a day of work, not a project:
  $ uv run -- benchbox run --official --seed 42 --platform duckdb --benchmark tpcds --scale 1
  41 seconds wall clock; 309/309 queries passed; benchmark.compliance_class = official;
  execution.official = true; phases.validation.status = PASSED and summary.validation = passed
  (consistent, unlike 112 of the 207 legacy corpus bundles); power_at_size = 256,866.
  Bundle: ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/results/tpcds_sf1_duckdb_sql_20260823_085826_fc9467d8.json

This supersedes any lingering doubt from tpcds-can-never-be-published-official-flag-not-wired: that item's remaining w2 is an integration TEST, and the classifier itself demonstrably works on develop as of 2026-08-23. The bundle above was produced by post-#1770 code, unlike the 2026-08-18 bundle that item warns about.

Two adversarial reviewers on 2026-08-23 independently agreed TPC-DS at SF1 is the highest-value corpus addition available and that SF10/SF100 should NOT gate it.

Customer framing: TPC-DS is advertised in the README benchmark catalogue and on the landing page, is the single most-searched benchmark in this category, and the public corpus has none of it. Maximum scale factor across the entire existing corpus is 1.0.

anti_patterns.dont: Block SF1 publication on SF10/SF100 capacity
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD ship SF1 and treat larger scales as the w3 decision
anti_patterns.why: SF1 takes under a minute per platform and SF100 needs dedicated hardware

anti_patterns.dont: Publish TPC-DS at SF0.01 or SF0.1 to close the gap quickly
anti_patterns.why: sub-scale TPC-DS is classified unofficial_subscale, is refused by submit, and is not the result readers are looking for
it was fixed in PR #1770 and re-verified end to end on 2026-08-23

anti_patterns.dont: add a single-platform cohort to results-data
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD run results-data/validate_corpus.py before opening any corpus PR; it is not part of pr-preflight, so a green preflight does not cover it
anti_patterns.why: results-data/validate_corpus.py exits 1 on any (benchmark, scale) cohort with fewer than 3 platforms, and PR #1854 added TPC-DS SF10 with DuckDB alone, which broke that invariant on develop

anti_patterns.dont: bundle this with the SF 0.1 expansion PR
anti_patterns.why: they answer different questions (depth-per-cohort vs benchmark-coverage) and reviewer attention shouldn't be split.
the choice has strategic implications (head-to-head with ClickBench vs broader TPC family); document the trade-off explicitly in w1.

anti_patterns.dont: treat TPC-DS corpus expansion as a Results Explorer launch blocker
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD publish TPC-DS in parallel after or with the v0.4.0 cut
anti_patterns.why: the curated preview is defined over the current corpus

anti_patterns.dont: use TPC-DS fractional scale factors below 1
anti_patterns.why: they violate CLAUDE.md's hard rule and produce non-standard, non-comparable results.

preserves.behavior: Cohort isolation per strategy doc - never compare across benchmark families.
Existing TPC-H and SSB cohorts untouched.
Maintainer-run trust label on all generated bundles.
Published TPC-DS bundles carry compliance_class=official and real validation, or they are not published at all

prior_art.concept: every committed cohort must have at least 3 platforms (hard validator gate)

work_units.evidence: TPC-DS confirmed; official DuckDB SF1 packaged via benchbox submit in PR #1786
work_units.notes:
Compare on three axes:
  1. Platform parity: which 3+ supported platforms can run it cleanly
     at SF 0.01? (DuckDB and DataFusion run both; Polars/SQLite vary.)
  2. Runtime + storage: TPC-DS has 99 queries; ClickBench has 43.
     Estimate wall-clock per cohort.
  3. Strategic value: TPC-DS aligns with the "TPC family" framing in
     the strategy doc; ClickBench creates direct head-to-head visibility.

Document the decision and rationale in
`_project/analysis/third-cohort-selection-<date>.md` and link it from
this TODO before starting w2.
work_units.summary: Confirm TPC-DS as the cohort (decision made 2026-08-17) and size the datagen and runtime budget

work_units.evidence:
PR #1859. TPC-DS SF10 cohort completed to 3 platforms; results-data/validate_corpus.py back to exit 0 with 'tpcds SF=10.0: 3 platforms ([DataFusion, DuckDB, Spark]) [OK]'. Corpus now 213 bundles.

  DuckDB      309/309  power@size 497,999
  DataFusion  309/309  power@size 151,089
  Spark       308/309  no power@size

Spark's single failure is honest and published rather than hidden: query 95 died after 2.2s with SparkOutOfMemoryError [UNABLE_TO_ACQUIRE_MEMORY] against the 4g default driver heap on a 16GB machine with a 10GB dataset -- a resource limit, not a correctness defect. The bundle records validation=partial and no power_at_size, so the Explorer excludes it from ranking with reason failed_queries and it cannot be read as a clean comparison. Re-running at a larger heap on the same 16GB machine would trade the OOM for swapping, which is a worse measurement, not a better one.

Follow-on from that finding: PR #1860 registers spark driver_memory as a real --platform-option. The adapter has read config.get('driver_memory') (default 4g) all along and add_cli_arguments documents --driver-memory, but it was never a registered option spec, so a user hitting this OOM had no lever. Same class as the thirteen keys declared in #1844.

work_units.evidence:
DECISION AND EXECUTION COMPLETE. PR #1854. DuckDB TPC-DS SF10, --official --seed 42: 309/309 passed, validation passed, compliance_class official, power@size 497,999 (SF1 was 269,803). Bundle validates clean; inventory row carries trust_label maintainer-run.

Decision recorded: SF10 yes, SF100 no for now. SF1 tells a reader how fast an engine is on this hardware; two points tell them how it scales, which is what a corpus is for. SF100 costs roughly ten times the runtime and ~100GB on disk for a third point that mostly confirms the trend, and can be added later without redoing either.

Scope: DuckDB only, not a repeat of the three-platform cohort. At SF1 DataFusion was 3.8x slower than DuckDB and Spark 42x, so a three-platform SF10 run is dominated by Spark's runtime to re-establish a ranking SF1 already shows. Cross-platform comparison lives at SF1; the scale ladder lives at SF10.

Sequencing respected: SF10 is its own branch off develop, so PR #1839 (SF1) is not delayed. Known consequence: results-data/corpus-inventory.json conflicts between #1839 and #1854; it is generated, so whichever lands second regenerates it. Also resolved that same conflict on #1839 against current develop (merge 680fd95eb) -- inventory regenerated to 210 bundles, all maintainer-run, pr-preflight 28042 passed.

Cleared a related risk: the three SF1 bundles carry no sidecar, and under the merged #1843 logic rule 4 a sidecar-less bundle defaults to maintainer-run. Verified on the merged branch: 210/210 maintainer-run. No bundle lands mislabelled.

selection memo.

work_units.evidence: Filed as sqlite-tpcds-fails-every-query-cursor-passed-as-connection (medium-high). Root cause measured, not assumed: every query fails with "'sqlite3.Cursor' object has no attribute 'cursor'" -- a Cursor reaching SQLiteAdapter.execute_query (benchbox/platforms/sqlite.py:530) where a Connection is expected. Adapter plumbing, not a SQL dialect limit; SQLite runs TPC-H fine. Reproduces in seconds at SF0.01 with a single query, so it is not scale-dependent. Second defect recorded in the same item: the bundle records error=null on every FAILED row, so the reason never leaves the console.
work_units.summary: SQLite fails all 103 TPC-DS queries at SF1 - file as its own defect, it is not a cohort blocker

work_units.evidence: Filed as dataframe-results-can-never-be-submitted-no-compliance-class (high). Root cause located: benchbox/core/runner/dataframe_runner.py:232-239 and benchbox/platforms/dataframe/benchmark_mixin.py:287-294 both construct BenchmarkInfoInput without compliance_class, and from benchmark_config rather than the benchmark instance, so PR #1770's config threading cannot reach them. Measured on the same benchmark down both paths: polars-df emits a benchmark block of only id/name/scale_factor/test_type with compliance_class ABSENT and validation not_run, while the SQL path emits unofficial_subscale. Refused twice over by submit (compliance class) and publish_admission (non-clean validation), so no DataFrame result can be published -- about half the corpus.
work_units.summary: polars-df completes 309/309 TPC-DS but the DataFrame path sets no compliance_class and runs no validation even under --official, so DataFrame results can never be submitted - file separately
